summary: Join our comprehensive training course on Impact Assessment in Rural Development. Equip yourself with essential tools to drive sustainable community growth.
lede: Impact assessment in rural development gives project professionals a practical way to distinguish completed activities from meaningful change in livelihoods, resilience, food security, access to services, and wellbeing. This course shows you how to build credible evidence that supports accountability and clearer communication with funders, government, and communities. You will develop a theory of change, define relevant indicators, plan baseline and endline studies, and combine quantitative evidence with stories from the field. You will then use your findings to guide decisions, strengthen project delivery, and support continuous improvement.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals who regularly monitor, evaluate, and report on rural development projects and programs, ensuring they can effectively demonstrate and communicate the impact of their interventions.
audience: Project and program managers in rural development
Government officers in agriculture, rural development, social
modules: Foundations of Impact Assessment in Rural Development
Developing Theories of Change and Results Frameworks
Baseline, Midline, and Endline Assessment Design
Using Impact Evidence for Learning and Adaptive Management
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of monitoring and evaluation concepts. Familiarity with rural development projects and a minimum of 2 years of professional experience in the sector are recommended.
